_readme: Canonical roster: which countries the fire channel tracks.
This is the INPUT to fetch_window_baseline.py, deliberately separate
from country_history.json which is its OUTPUT. Before 2026-07-30 the
refresh iterated its own previous output, so a country that failed one
run was absent from the next run input and was never retried. The set
could only shrink. Algeria, Iraq, Mexico and Namibia were lost that
way on 2026-07-30, Algeria while carrying the highest year-to-date
burnt-area anomaly in the set at 14.2x, and nothing reported it.
Seeded from a global VIIRS sweep ranked by detections, then edited by
hand. Adding a country here is all that is needed; the next refresh

Greece, Portugal and Morocco added 2026-07-30 on Kristjan: the original sweep ranked by detection count in one week, which under-selects a Mediterranean country whose season had not opened. A roster chosen by one weeks volume is not a roster for a season.

Forest-first expansion 2026-07-31 on Kristjan: target forest fire countries rather than savanna, since savanna is most of the missing VOLUME but almost none of the missing STORIES, being fuel-limited, agricultural and near-incapable of clearing an anomaly gate. Balkan and Mediterranean entries are small in hectares and kept anyway: that is where the 2026 anomaly is, with the Mediterranean EU at 1.9x for July.

NOT added, pending a separate decision: Myanmar 4.3M ha, India 4.0M, Thailand 2.7M, Laos 2.6M, Cambodia 1.5M, Vietnam 284k. Roughly 15.5M ha, three times our European coverage, but substantially crop-residue and swidden burning on a Feb-Apr calendar rather than forest fire. Same objection as savanna in a different form.

EU-27 completed 2026-08-03 on Kristjan. Several members have almost no fire (Malta, Luxembourg, Ireland, Netherlands, Denmark) and will never clear the gate. They are tracked anyway because D-043 names a US and European reader, and a reader who cannot find their own country has no reason to trust the ones they can. Coverage of readers, not of hectares.

South and Southeast Asia added the same day: Myanmar, India, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Syria. Roughly 15.5M ha, three times our European coverage. Their burning is substantially crop residue and swidden on a Feb-Apr calendar rather than closed-canopy forest fire, so expect them to behave like the savanna set: large, regular, and rarely anomalous. Tracked because volume that large should not be invisible, not because it is expected to produce stories.
